title: He Built a Game Alone and Sold It for $2.5 Billion #shorts
description:
In 2009 a Swedish programmer started a small side project. Five years later Microsoft paid two and a half billion dollars for it. The story of Minecraft and Markus Persson.
Follow for more true stories of fortunes made and lost.

lines.text: He built a video game alone, and sold it for two and a half billion dollars.
In two thousand and nine, Markus Persson was a Swedish programmer with a day job.
At night, he worked on a strange side project.
A game made of blocks, with no real goal.
He just put an early version online and let people pay to play.
They told their friends. Then their friends told theirs.
Within a few years, Minecraft was one of the biggest games on Earth.
His tiny studio, Mojang, had around forty employees.
Then, in two thousand and fourteen, Microsoft made an offer.
Two and a half billion dollars.
Today Minecraft has sold over three hundred million copies, the best-selling game ever.
